work: Escort a truck through the park
hazards: Crane lifts — buildings and toilets
Exclusion zone under the hook goes up; ground checked — in doubt, stop and ask. Nobody walks or stands under a suspended building. Licensed dogger and operator; no lift when wind exceeds the chart.
SWMS TSV500.1 · crane install
Forklift — unloading, loading, carrying
LF licence, pre-start done. Spotter in the Safe Zone, out of the line of fire. Loads restrained, never one on one. Reverse when the load blocks the view. Anyone in the zone: stop, lower, brake.
SEQ-SWMS-009.01g · steps 2, 6
Jacking and levelling — the supervisor checks it first
Never under a building on jacks unless on an approved support; watch jacks for pressure. Pushers place the packers, hands out of pinch points. Operator stays in the seat while it is on the tynes.
SWMS TSV500.1 · jacking, levelling
Blocks and packers and the 20 kg limit
Two-person lift or the forklift; work to the lay-down plan. No body part between skids and ground. Cut-5 gloves; never lift with snakes sitting under packers. Bite kit on the truck.
SWMS TSV500.1 · blocks
Stairs and landings
Stairs to AS 1657, fitted and fixed before anyone uses the building; treads and handrails checked. No building is handed over without its steps — tick Steps installed in the page.
SWMS TSV500.1 · the page
Spotting — every load, every reverse
One named spotter, agreed hand signals before the lift, and never inside the line of fire. If the spotter loses sight of the load or the driver loses sight of the spotter, everything stops.
SEQ-SWMS-009.01g · steps 2, 6
Water barriers — moving and placing

Drained before they move unless the plan says otherwise; a full barrier is a different lift. Placed to the barrier drawing, not by eye. Hands clear of the joins; never straddle a barrier being pushed.
SWMS TSV500.1 · iEDM key plan K220
Driving the track and Macintosh Park

40 km/h on track, 10 km/h in Macintosh Park. Pre-set routes; follow the traffic controllers. Beacon on; give way to pedestrians and plant. Nobody drives through the park unescorted — a truck waits at the gate.
D007-26003-02 · 009.01g · Crane driver rule
Escorting a truck

Escort leads on the agreed route at a pace the truck can hold, beacon on; the driver follows the escort, not the sat-nav. Slow right down near the public — they have right of way. Light rail zone: permit first.
009.01g · iEDM rules · SEQ-RM-010d
Trucks — tray access and restraint
Fall controls before anyone gets on a tray. Rated straps or chains on every load. A building leaves only with its pre-transit checklist done — doors and loose items secured, aircons restrained.
SAF-PRO-075 · TRAN-WI-R1.2 · 009.01g
Take 5 — before every task

Stop and do a Take 5 before each new task and again whenever the job or the conditions change — a new drop, a new spot, a new crew member, rain, a crowd. Two minutes, every time: it is the Coates risk assessment tool at the task.
Coates Take 5 · Life Saving Rule: Risk Assessment · added 27 Sep 2026
Congested areas and low branches

The precinct is busy — public, other contractors, event vehicles and the tram. Walk the route before the truck does, walking pace, barricade the drop spot. Look up before every lift and every move: branches, awnings, signs, wires.
SEQ-SWMS-009.01g · walk the route first · added 27 Sep 2026
Tight spots

Plan the placement before the unit arrives: measure the gap, clear the path, a spotter on every tight manoeuvre, hands out of pinch points. If it does not fit as planned, stop and re-plan — never force it.
SWMS TSV500.1 · the placement plan · added 27 Sep 2026
High communication at all times
Radio or phone on and charged. Say what you are about to do before you do it; one voice directs each lift and each reverse; any change to the plan goes to the whole crew straight away.
Site communication · contacts under 08 · added 27 Sep 2026
rules: iEDM site induction done — every person, before starting
Site hours 07:00–17:00 Monday to Friday unless iEDM approves otherwise
Report to the Coates contact and site office on arrival
WC · LF · DG · RA · C1 · CV · WP — held by the person doing it
Crane Lift Plan · Traffic Management Plan · Permit to Work
Pre-transit checklist TRAN-WI-R1.2 · SAF-PRO-075 for every move
Power on by a licensed electrician only — test & tag, RCD
Record it in the page: arrival, levelled, steps, photos, numbers
Water, hat, breaks · spotter near the public · report it straight away
Take 5 before every new task, and again when anything changes
PPE on before the gate: hi-vis, hard hat, glasses, gloves, boots, long sleeves, sun
SWMS reviewed together before work starts — today’s task not in it, stop
Unsure? Ask the question. Everyone has the right to stop the job
life: I will not commence any work that I am unfamiliar with, that is non-routine, potentially hazardous or impacted by changing conditions without first completing the appropriate Coates risk assessment tool to identify, assess and control risks.
I will not commence any High-Risk Work without a risk assessment being completed and without having signed onto the applicable Safe Work Method Statement (SWMS).
I will be inducted, trained, competent andhold the required certification and licences to conduct the task.

When I commence work, I will be physically fit, and not impaired by fatigue, injury, distraction, drugs or alcohol. I will wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE) as identified for the task or site rules.

I will only use tools and equipment that are fit for purpose and for which I am trained, competent and authorised. I will ensure that damaged or defective equipment is tagged out and removed from service.

When I commence a work activity related to a Coates Top 10 Critical Risk, I will always ensure that I review and strictly adhere to the non-negotiable rules and controls for that Critical Risk to protect me, my workmates and others from serious harm.
